answer: A tight ring of 105 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Because the dune calculation reruns each epoch, the comet weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the lagoon settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 26% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 28 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
